paper.title_en: Universal Nonpower Law Scaling from a Chaotic Renormalization Group in the Harper-Hofstadter Model
paper.abstract_en: Previous studies of incommensurate systems concluded that their critical scaling is sensitively dependent on the irrational, <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math>, which determines the incommensuration. Contrary to this belief, in the canonical Harper-Hofstadter model, we show there is universal <math display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>-independent scaling for almost all <math display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>. This critical scaling is characterized by non-power-law time-length scaling <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>∼</mo><msup><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>ζ</mi><mi>log</mi><mi>log</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math>. We demonstrate this in the superfluid fraction of a Bose gas, and the specific heat of a Fermi gas. This scaling is generic of a broad class of generalized Harper-Hofstadter models. The <math display="inline"><mi>α</mi></math>-independent scaling emerges as the number theoretic properties of almost all irrational numbers are statistically identical (à la Gauss-Kuzmin statistics). Consequently, we conjecture similar <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>α</mi></mrow></math>-independent scaling applies in incommensurate models more generally.
